'''Viswanathan Sasisekharan''' (born 1933) is an Indian biophysicist known for his work on the structure and conformation of [[biopolymer]]s. He introduced the use of torsion angles to describe [[polypeptide]] and [[protein]] conformation, a central principle of the (φ, ψ) plot (later known as the [[Ramachandran plot]]).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Sasisekharan|first=V|title=Stereochemical Criteria for Polypeptide and Protein Structures|work=Collagen|publisher=John Wiley|year=1962|editor-last=Ramanathan|editor-first=N|location=New York|pages=39–77}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Ramachandran|first1=G. N.|last2=Ramakrishnan|first2=C.|last3=Sasisekharan|first3=V.|date=1963|title=Stereochemistry of polypeptide chain configurations|journal=Journal of Molecular Biology|volume=7|pages=95–99|doi=10.1016/s0022-2836(63)80023-6|issn=0022-2836|pmid=13990617}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Hollingsworth|first1=Scott A.|last2=Karplus|first2=P. Andrew|date=2010-10-01|title=A fresh look at the Ramachandran plot and the occurrence of standard structures in proteins|journal=BioMolecular Concepts|volume=1|issue=3–4|pages=271–283|doi=10.1515/bmc.2010.022|issn=1868-503X|pmc=3061398|pmid=21436958}}</ref> Additionally, he was the first to introduce alternative models of DNA structure that provided insights beyond the standard [[Nucleic acid double helix|double helix]] model.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Sasisekharan|first1=V|last2=Pattabiraman|first2=N|date=1976|title=Double stranded polynucleotides: two typical alternative conformations for nucleic acids|url=https://www.currentscience.ac.in/cs/Downloads/article_id_045_22_0779_0783_0.pdf|journal=Current Science|volume=45|pages=779–783|access-date=21 June 2020|archive-date=13 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213033536/https://www.currentscience.ac.in/cs/Downloads/article_id_045_22_0779_0783_0.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Sasisekharan|first1=V.|last2=Pattabiraman|first2=N.|date=1978|title=Structure of DNA predicted from stereochemistry of nucleoside derivatives|url=http://www.nature.com/articles/275159a0|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=275|issue=5676|pages=159–162|doi=10.1038/275159a0|pmid=692688|bibcode=1978Natur.275..159S|s2cid=4145327|issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Sasisekharan|first1=V.|last2=Pattabiraman|first2=N.|last3=Gupta|first3=G.|date=1978-09-01|title=Some implications of an alternative structure for DNA.|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=75|issue=9|pages=4092–4096|doi=10.1073/pnas.75.9.4092|issn=0027-8424|pmc=336057|pmid=279899|bibcode=1978PNAS...75.4092S|doi-access=free}}</ref> For his contributions to the biological sciences, he was awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of India’s highest science awards, in 1978.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=19 September 2016}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
V. Sasisekharan was born on 28 June 1933 in the South Indian state of [[Tamil Nadu]]. He earned his Ph.D. from the [[University of Madras]] in 1959.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Sasisekharan">{{cite web|date=2016|title=Indian Fellow - Sasisekharan|url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N80-0706|access-date=23 September 2016|publisher=Indian National Science Academy|archive-date=25 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925015242/http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N80-0706|url-status=dead}}</ref> From 1959–1963, he was a lecturer at the University of Madras, and from 1963–1964, he was a visiting scientist at the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIDDK).<ref name="Indian Fellow - Sasisekharan" /> In 1964, he joined the University of Madras as a reader at the Centre of Advanced Study in Physics and served as a professor and administrative head of the Department of Physics from 1968–1970 and 1971–1972.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Sasisekharan" /> He was a visiting professor at [[Princeton University]] at their Frick Chemical Laboratory from 1970–1971.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Sasisekharan" />

In 1972, Sasisekharan moved to the [[Indian Institute of Science]] (IISc) Bangalore, where he served as the professor and chairman of the [http://mbu.iisc.ac.in/ Molecular Biophysics Unit]; chairman of the Division of Chemical and Biological Sciences; and dean of the Faculty of Science. He was a visiting professor at the [[University of Chicago]], and was an adjunct professor at the School of Pharmacy, [[University of California, San Francisco]].<ref name="Pharmacy1979">{{cite book|author=University of California, San Francisco. School of Pharmacy|title=UCSF School of Pharmacy Bulletin|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hPw2AQAAMAAJ&pg=RA4-PA45|year=1979|publisher=The University.|pages=4–}}</ref>

== Research ==
As a graduate student, Sasisekharan studied the structure of [[collagen]] chains and developed methods to generate the coordinates of constituent atoms of peptides with a high degree of accuracy.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sasisekharan|first=V|date=1959|title=Structure of collagen and related compounds|journal=PhD Thesis, University of Madras}}</ref> Using this approach and published crystal structures, he identified allowable non-bonded distances between atoms of consecutive amino acids.<ref name=":0" /> For the first time, he used torsion angles to describe the conformation of polypeptide chains  and determined the allowable regions for the two torsion angles (originally named φ and φ’, later as φ and ψ).<ref name=":0" /> This formed the basis for the (φ, ψ) plot, which was expanded and later became known as the [[Ramachandran plot]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Citation|last1=Ramachandran|first1=G.N.|chapter=Conformation of Polypeptides and Proteins|date=1968|chapter-url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0065323308604027|title=Advances in Protein Chemistry|volume=23|pages=283–437|publisher=Elsevier|language=en|doi=10.1016/s0065-3233(08)60402-7|isbn=978-0-12-034223-5|access-date=2020-06-21|last2=Sasisekharan|first2=V.|pmid=4882249|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref> While Sasisekharan calculated these allowable regions using only a few available protein [[Protein Crystallography|crystal structures]] at the time, the (φ, ψ) plot has remained nearly unchanged for 60 years.<ref name=":2" />

Later in his career, part of Sasisekharan’s work focused on the structure of nucleic acids. He and his coworkers demonstrated that the available experimental results were compatible with both right- and left-handed double helical models for DNA. They also showed the enormous degree of conformational flexibility in the basic units of DNA and highlighted the concept of sequence specific conformation and DNA conformational polymorphism. In addition, they proposed a structure of DNA consisting of alternating left- and right-handed helical segments, known as the side-by-side (S-B-S) model, an alternative to the right-handed double helix model.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> The S-B-S model offered greater structural flexibility that could facilitate the uncoiling of the double helix without topological rearrangement during replication or other processes.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bansal|first=Manju|date=2003|title=DNA structure: Revisiting the Watson–Crick double helix|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/24110017|journal=Current Science|volume=85|issue=11|pages=1556–1563|jstor=24110017|issn=0011-3891}}</ref>

His son, [[Ram Sasisekharan]], is a bioengineer<ref name="Sugary route to success">{{cite web | url=http://www.telegraphindia.com/1130610/jsp/knowhow/story_16989842.jsp#.V-U47Zh97IU | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130615235749/http://www.telegraphindia.com/1130610/jsp/knowhow/story_16989842.jsp#.V-U47Zh97IU | url-status=dead | archive-date=15 June 2013 | title=Sugary route to success | publisher=The Telegraph | date=10 June 2013 | first=T.V. | last=Jayan | access-date=26 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Ram Sasisekharan, PhD {{!}} MIT Department of Biological Engineering|url=https://be.mit.edu/directory/ram-sasisekharan|access-date=2020-06-21|website=be.mit.edu|language=en}}</ref> and a co-author of some of his publications.<ref>{{cite book|title=Fundamentals of Advanced Omics Technologies: From Genes to Metabolites|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=s75CAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA280|date=14 February 2014|publisher=Newnes|isbn=978-0-444-62670-7|pages=280–}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded Sasisekharan the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]] (one of India’s highest science awards) in 1978 for his contributions to the fields of biopolymers and DNA structure analysis.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees" /> He received the FICCI Award of the [[Federation of Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry]] in 1981, and the [[Indian National Science Academy]] awarded him the Jagadis Chandra Bose Medal in 1983.<ref name="The Jagadis Chandra Bose Medal">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#34 | title=The Jagadis Chandra Bose Medal | publisher=INSA | date=2016 | access-date=24 September 2016 | archive-date=16 September 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#34 | url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1985, he held the ASTRA chair in Biological Sciences at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] and received the Jagdish Chandra Bose Award for Research in Life Sciences from the [[University Grants Commission of India]].<ref name="Indian Fellow - Sasisekharan" /> He was awarded the Honor Summus Medal of the Watunull Foundation in 1987 and was selected as a Fogarty Scholar-In-Residence at the [[National Institutes of Health]] in 1988. He received the [[Om Prakash Bhasin Award]] in 1989.<ref name="OPB Awards">{{cite web | url=http://www.opbfawards.com/biotechnology.html | title=OPB Awards | publisher=Om Prakash Bhasin Foundation | date=2014 | access-date=23 September 2016 | archive-date=6 November 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106195352/http://www.opbfawards.com/biotechnology.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> Sasisekharan was elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] in 1969<ref name="Fellow Profile">{{cite web|date=2016|title=Fellow Profile|url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Sasisekharan,_Prof._Vishwanathan|access-date=24 September 2016|publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 1980.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Sasisekharan" />
